senses.vi: khả năng nhận biết; trực giác

thesaurus.definition: measuring instrument in which the echo of a pulse of microwave radiation is used to detect and locate distant objects

examples: They were able to find the enemy fleet using radar.
wiktionary.gloss: In full primary radar: a method of detecting a distant object and determining its position, velocity, or other characteristics by analysing radio waves (usually microwaves) which are sent towards the object and which reflect off its surfaces; also, the field of study of this method.

In full secondary radar: a method of detecting a distant object and determining its position, velocity, or other characteristics by analysing signals transmitted by the object in response to radio waves sent towards the object.

examples: The Ministry of Defence funded the development of an entirely new radar and improved avionics.
wiktionary.gloss: Often preceded by a descriptive word: a system using one of the above detection methods, differentiated by configuration or platform, frequency, power, and other technical attributes.

examples: Each of these aircraft has been upgraded with a new radar and a more powerful engine.
wiktionary.gloss: An installation of the apparatus for operating one of the above detection systems.

Often preceded by a descriptive word: a natural (for example, in an animal such as a bat) or human-made detection method based on the analysis of reflected signals other than radio waves, as light waves or sound waves; (countable) an instance of this.

examples: His sensitive radar for hidden alliances keeps him out of trouble.
wiktionary.gloss: A superior ability to detect something; an awareness, an intuition.

blocks.etymology: The noun is derived from RADAR by anacronymic evolution. RADAR is an acronym of ra(dio) d(etection) a(nd) r(anging) which was coined by Lieutenant-Commander Samuel M. Tucker and Lieutenant-Commander F. R. Furth of the United States Navy in November 1940. The verb is probably derived from the noun.

wiktionary.gloss: To use a radar apparatus (noun senses 1, 1.1, or 2) on (someone or something); to scan (someone or something) with, or as if with, radar.

idioms.gloss: Without attracting notice; in an undetected or secretive manner.
To go unnoticed, especially for a long period of time.
Within someone's awareness, attention or consideration.
Unlikely to happen or be important in the near future, or tending to escape detection or attention.
To vanish or fall into obscurity; to become forgotten or ignored.
Likely to happen, or be important in the near future or tending to attract attention.
Synonym of fly under the radar
Synonym of drop off the radar.
